claims.text: The ability of lightweight high-entropy alloys to combine low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance is primarily mediated by a stable, refined microstructure with high grain-boundary density.
Systematic variation of alloying elements and processing conditions can produce the proposed stable, refined microstructure.
The proposed test alloy has a nominal CoCrFeMnNi composition in an as-cast or wrought state.
Adding Ti, Al, or Cu may optimize the alloy's microstructure and properties.
Heat treatment, mechanical alloying, or spark-plasma sintering may optimize the alloy's microstructure and properties.
A high density of grain boundaries impedes dislocation movement.
A high density of grain boundaries impedes crack propagation.
A high density of grain boundaries impedes corrosion penetration.
The proposed grain-boundary effects enhance mechanical strength.
The proposed grain-boundary effects enhance corrosion resistance.
The proposed grain-boundary effects enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The modified high-entropy alloy is predicted to have 20% higher yield strength than Inconel 718 under the same test conditions.
The modified high-entropy alloy is predicted to have a 30% lower corrosion rate than Inconel 718 under the same test conditions.
The modified high-entropy alloy is predicted to have a 25% lower oxidation rate than Inconel 718 under the same test conditions.
Above 1000°C, grain-boundary and microstructural instability may cause the proposed mechanism to cease to hold.
In acidic or high-salinity environments, grain-boundary and microstructural instability may cause the proposed mechanism to cease to hold.
